rules.source: Every number on this page is read from {module} — the same module the engine uses.
rules.derived: Nothing here was typed by hand, so nothing here can drift from the game.

rarity.title: Rarity
rarity.note: rarity.ts — derived from the base stat total
rarity.foot: The thresholds come from the dex percentile and not from round numbers: most species are final evolutions, and a ladder of round values would make {rare} the biggest tier in the game. Foil starts at rare.

packs.title: Packs
packs.note: packs.ts — {count} cards, drawn from a seed
packs.foot: Pity counts packs without an ultra or above; on the last one the rare+ slot becomes a guaranteed ultra and the count resets. Shiny rolls on any card and turns it foil.

forge.title: Dust and forge
forge.note: dust.ts — a duplicate turns into dust, dust buys the card you pick
forge.foot: A ×{ratio} ratio the whole way up: four duplicates of a tier pay for one card of that tier. The forge is what makes the dex completable — the long tail does not close by drawing packs.

battle.title: Battle
battle.note: damage.ts · engine.ts — fixed Lv{level} on both sides, IV {iv} and EV 0
battle.ratios: {ad} is {physical} on a physical move and {special} on a special one. Effectiveness comes from the {types}×{types} matrix; a dual type multiplies, so ×4 and ×¼ exist.

steps.order: Move priority; a tie is resolved by {stat}; a tie on {stat} {seed}.
steps.blocked: Prevention — asleep does not act, paralysed loses the turn {chance} of the time.
steps.hit: Hit — the accuracy of the move is rolled.
steps.pp: PP decrements; {struggle}, which spends no PP and hurts whoever uses it.
steps.struggle: at zero that slot becomes Struggle
steps.residual: End of turn — burn, poison, and then the faint check.

battle.moves: Each Pokémon carries {slots} moves, picked for type coverage and not for raw power.
battle.potion: Item: one {potion} per side per battle, restoring {heal} of max HP. | Item: {count} {potion} per side per battle, restoring {heal} of max HP.
battle.rematch: Losing costs nothing — the rematch is immediate.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.note: status.ts — one at a time, they do not stack
conditions.paralysis: {stat} ×{factor} and a {chance} chance to lose the turn.
conditions.burn: Physical attack ×{factor} and {fraction} of max HP per turn.
conditions.sleep: Does not act for {min} to {max} turns, drawn at random.
conditions.foot: Freeze is left out on purpose: it is frustrating to receive and not very interesting to apply.

league.title: The League
league.note: gyms.ts — {count} leaders, one per generation, unlocked in order
league.foot: Every Pokémon on a team carries the leader's type {and} comes from their generation — winning in order walks through the generations. The last one on the team is the ace, the highest BST. The leader's AI is greedy with noise that falls from {first} in the first gym to {last} in the last; the potion arrives at gym {potion} and the matchup switch at {swap}.

economy.title: Economy
economy.note: economy.ts — where the coins come from
economy.foot: The whole campaign pays {coins} — about {packs}. The rematch exists because without it income after the last gym would drop to one pack a day, forever. The flawless bonus is about what is being paid, so on a rematch it follows the rematch.

rules.end: There is no tutorial screen, and that is on purpose: the interface teaches at the point of decision — the move button shows effectiveness before you pick, the deck builder marks who {weakness}, and the shop puts the rates next to the price. This page is the reference to check afterwards, not the gate before.
